text:
jess_support: Heads-up — customer reporting structured-output / JSON mode fncall failures. They say our runtime rejects the call with "InvalidFunctionArguments: items must be an array" even though their payload looks valid. Also seeing a 401 spike behind their proxy.

maria_customer: repro attached — SDK v1.12.1, JSON mode enabled. We send payload from our backend proxy. Works locally sometimes, fails in production. Error: "400 Invalid arguments" + body: "{\"error\":\"InvalidFunctionArguments\",\"message\":\"items: expected array\"}"

sam_swe: Can you paste the exact function schema and the request body you submitted? Quick guess: shape drift — maybe they sent an object map instead of an array.

maria_customer: copy of request (sanitized):

```json
{"model":"x-redwood-1","json_mode":true,"function_call":{"name":"processOrder","arguments":{
  "order_id":"ORD-123",
  "items": {"SKU123":"2","SKU456":"1"}
}}
```

sam_swe: there it is — schema expected: items: [ {sku:string, qty:int} ]. Customer is sending items as an object map (sku->qty). That will fail strict JSON-mode validation. Why does it sometimes pass locally? Possibly our proxy auto-coercion in some paths or SDK client-side upgrade.

jess_support: logs from their production request show our gateway received Content-Type: application/json and body as above. runtime returned 400. infra_bot noticed 401s around the same window:

```
[infra_bot] 3301239999 -> 3301240003: 401 proxy-auth failure for connection from 34.82.10.12
[runtime] 3301240001: 400 InvalidFunctionArguments items: expected array got object
```

ops_oncall: Is the 401 coming from their upstream proxy OR our internal auth? If their proxy strips Authorization, that could cause different code paths (we have fallback behavior that tries lenient parsing when auth missing).

sam_swe: steps to reproduce (what I ran locally):
1) curl to our hosted endpoint with JSON-mode and a function schema expecting items as array.
2) send items as object map.
3) observe 400.

Example curl I used:

```bash
curl -sS -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"x-redwood-1","json_mode":true,"function_call":{"name":"processOrder","arguments":{"order_id":"ORD-123","items":{"SKU123":2}}}}'
```

Got: "400 InvalidFunctionArguments: items must be array"

sam_swe: workaround for them is to coerce map->array before sending, but we should surface a clearer error message and offer a transformation hook or accept map shapes with a compatibility flag.

maria_customer: we can't easily change our proxy right now (it normalizes and signs requests). Any way you can relax validation on our tenant temporarily? We're blocked for an urgent checkout flow.

jess_support: I can open a temporary tolerance flag for their org while we advise dev to update payload. Need ticket and approval.

runtime_team: tagging you for runtime validation policy — is there precedent to accept {sku:qty} maps as compatible with items array in JSON-mode when schema clearly expects array? Risk: ambiguous ordering, type mapping.

runtime_team: short answer — automatic coercion is risky, but we can add a tenant-level compatibility shim that will transform an object map into items array using keys as sku and parse ints. It requires a small change to the JSON-mode validation layer and a feature flag. Estimate ~2d to implement + canary.

ops_oncall: also please investigate the 401s. If their proxy intermittently strips Authorization header we should not change behavior path based on auth presence — we should keep validation consistent.

sam_swe: plan: (1) support will ask customer to push a short-lived change to proxy to convert items map->array (sample snippet attached). (2) runtime team to schedule compatibility shim behind a tenant feature flag (ticket RT-4821). (3) infra to trace 401 spike and confirm source.

jess_support: sample shim snippet we can give to customer (node):

```js
// convert items map to array
function normalizeItems(body){
  if(body.function_call?.arguments?.items && !Array.isArray(body.function_call.arguments.items)){
    const map = body.function_call.arguments.items;
    body.function_call.arguments.items = Object.keys(map).map(k=>({sku:k, qty: parseInt(map[k],10)}));
  }
  return body;
}
```

maria_customer: thanks, we'll try that and report back. If we still hit 401s I'll paste gateway logs.

jess_support: opened support ticket SUP-2026-334, assigned to sam_swe + runtime_team. I'll add the temporary tenant tolerance note once we have approvals. Keeping thread open for updates. :thumbsup:
